issue.title: Duplicate dict key trips ruff F601 in the ownership audit test, blocking every commit repo-wide
issue.description:
REPRODUCTION (clean origin/master a0b6cd16b, no local changes):

    .venv/bin/ruff check tests/test_agent_artifact_directory_operation_audit.py
    F601 Dictionary key literal repeated
       --> tests/test_agent_artifact_directory_operation_audit.py:292:5

ROOT CAUSE: _REVIEWED_DIR_OPERATION_CONTEXTS contains the key
'src/sase/workspace_provider/reset_replay.py:_clear_owned_paths' TWICE, at lines 279 and
292, with different exemption prose. The second entry was added by b82f21c1b 'test:
register ownership audit coverage' (from the now-closed epic sase-mq) on top of an entry
that already existed. The second entry is also out of keep-sorted order, sitting after
the utils.py key.

IMPACT: this project sets commit_hooks.before: 'just fix' in sase/sase.yml. 'just fix'
runs 'ruff check --fix src/ tests/', F601 has no autofix, so the recipe exits 1 and the
before-commit hook fails. Every 'sase stitch create' / sase_git_commit in this repo
fails for every agent until this is fixed, regardless of what the agent changed. There
is no sanctioned bypass: sase stitch create has no hook-skip flag, the commit workflow
reads no skip env var, and project-local config has the highest merge precedence so a
user-global override cannot neutralize it. Discovered when a documentation-only refresh
could not be committed.

FIX: delete one of the two entries. Note that Python already discards the FIRST one, so
deleting line 279's entry preserves current runtime behavior exactly and is
semantically a no-op; deleting line 292's entry instead CHANGES which exemption the
audit enforces. The two exemptions say materially different things (line 279: 'Clears
only caller-supplied paths after resolving and verifying each path is inside the live
leased checkout...'; line 292: 'Clears only caller-supplied generated paths after
reset-and-replay has authorized a live leased checkout...'), so a human should confirm
which text is authoritative rather than deleting arbitrarily. Restore keep-sorted order
for the surviving entry.

VERIFY: 'just fix' exits 0, and
tests/test_agent_artifact_directory_operation_audit.py::test_artifact_directory_operation_sites_are_reviewed
still passes.

payload.entry: RELATED: sase-n1 — same file and same dict key. sase-n1 reports the entry MISSING (audit test failed); this bead reports it present TWICE (ruff F601). Whoever fixes either should read both, since the surviving entry must satisfy sase-n1's review requirement.
